results.finding: Empirical IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg 8-hourly, adjusted for renal function, should be started in suspected encephalitis; it can be stopped when an alternative diagnosis is established, or when HSV PCR is negative on CSF taken 72 hours or more after onset and the imaging and CSF findings do not suggest HSV encephalitis.

results.finding: Recommends CSF HSV PCR in all patients with suspected encephalitis and repeat testing when an early first sample is negative and HSV encephalitis remains clinically likely.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 IgG positive (titre 1:40), read with the CSF; moderate hyponatraemia (sodium 128 mEq/L); thyroid, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up: blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV and a cell-based serum anti-GluN1 IgG assay read together with the CSF result
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, endocrine and infectious contributors and pairs the serum antibody with the decisive CSF assay; here it uncovers moderate hyponatraemia.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Bilateral left-predominant medial temporal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion, haemorrhage or enhancement
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Lymphocytic pleocytosis (21 cells/uL), elevated IgG index and CSF-restricted oligoclonal bands; HSV-1/2 PCR negative; CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:80)
action_criteria.label: Analyse CSF for cells, protein and glucose, oligoclonal bands or IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay
action_criteria.rationale: The CSF anti-GluN1 cell-based assay is the decisive test (Graus 2016 definite criteria), and HSV PCR addresses the infectious mimic that must not be missed.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Diffuse slowing with bitemporal rhythmic delta (left more than right); no seizure or extreme delta brush on the routine record
action_criteria.label: Obtain an EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, including extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An abnormal EEG is one of the Graus 2016 supporting findings, and the automatisms need electrographic characterisation after two convulsions.

action_criteria.label: Screen for a testicular germ-cell tumour with scrotal ultrasound
action_criteria.rationale: Tumours are rare in men with anti-NMDAR encephalitis, but a testicular germ-cell tumour is the one to look for under 45, and its removal would be part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG to quantify seizure burden while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist
action_criteria.rationale: Two convulsions, a GCS of 12 and ongoing automatisms call for continuous monitoring to detect non-convulsive seizures.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum osmolality 264 mOsm/kg with urine osmolality 388 mOsm/kg and urine sodium 41 mmol/L
action_criteria.label: Measure serum and urine osmolality (with urine sodium) to characterise the hyponatraemia
action_criteria.rationale: Sodium below 130 mEq/L needs its own work-up; low serum osmolality with inappropriately concentrated urine and urine sodium above 30 mmol/L defines SIADH before fluid restriction or hypertonic saline.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Zopiclone adds sedation to benzodiazepines; no interaction changes first-line therapy
action_criteria.label: Check the patient's medications against the drugs the acute plan needs (aciclovir, corticosteroids, IVIG, antiseizure medication)
action_criteria.rationale: No interaction here changes the first-line plan; the check confirms that zopiclone should not be combined with lorazepam.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: General published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.label: Optionally review published evidence on anti-NMDAR encephalitis diagnosis and immunotherapy
action_criteria.rationale: Background reading only; no diagnostic or management step depends on it.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1-2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV aciclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).
Scrotal ultrasound shows no tumour; no further tumour imaging is needed unless the course is atypical or refractory.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam (continue maintenance after the loading dose) or lacosamide; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to the ICU / neurocritical care for a GCS of 12 after recurrent seizures, with airway assessment and cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation and insomnia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first rather than antipsychotics, and stop zopiclone to avoid combined sedation.
Treat the moderate hyponatraemia (128 mEq/L) as SIADH (no thiazide or SSRI on his medication list): fluid restriction, correcting by no more than 10 mEq/L in 24 hours.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioural management.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

accepted: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, tumour-negative (idiopathic), male patient

differential.key_features: CSF HSV-1/2 PCR negative three weeks after onset; bilateral medial temporal signal without haemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B or AMPA receptor)
differential.key_features: Serum neuronal-surface panel negative (LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA) and onconeural antibodies negative; hyponatraemia and limbic signal also fit LGI1, but CSF anti-GluN1 is positive.

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (depression with psychotic features)
differential.key_features: Convulsions, automatisms, echolalia, bitemporal electrographic seizures and CSF pleocytosis with oligoclonal bands are not explained by a primary psychiatric disorder.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced encephalopathy, NMS or serotonin syndrome
differential.key_features: Only zopiclone; no antipsychotic or serotonergic drug, so the ankle clonus is not serotonin toxicity; temperature 37.9 C, normal tone, CK 212 U/L after two convulsions.

key_clinical_evidence: Three weeks of subacute memory and behavioural change, echolalia, two convulsions, stereotyped hand movements and reduced consciousness (GCS 12): five of the six Graus 2016 groups.
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titre 1:80) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016); serum positive (1:40) is read with the CSF.

MRI shows bilateral left-predominant medial temporal FLAIR signal without restricted diffusion or haemorrhage; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds of patients and here excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes.
Routine EEG shows diffuse slowing with bitemporal rhythmic delta, and continuous EEG captures bitemporal seizures; extreme delta brush is absent, which excludes nothing.

Scrotal ultrasound shows no tumour: tumours are rare in men, and no further tumour imaging is needed unless the course is atypical. Moderate hyponatraemia (128 mEq/L, SIADH pattern) needs its own correction.
Earlier immunotherapy and tumour removal are associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis alongside the psychiatric change mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before a psychiatric diagnosis is accepted.
red_herrings.data_point: Personality change with irritability, suspicion, poor sleep and low mood in a previously well young man, first attributed to work stress and treated by the GP.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatraemia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: NMS requires antipsychotic exposure with lead-pipe rigidity, hyperthermia and markedly elevated CK; he has had no antipsychotic, and a CK of 212 U/L reflects two convulsions.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Raises concern for rhabdomyolysis or neuroleptic malignant syndrome.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis affects men too: about one in five patients in the largest cohort was male (Titulaer 2013). Tumours are rare in men, but the clinical syndrome is the same.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anti-NMDAR encephalitis excluded based on sex ('this is a female condition')

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: HSV encephalitis typically gives asymmetric temporal and insular signal with restricted diffusion and sometimes haemorrhage; here the changes are non-haemorrhagic without restricted diffusion, and CSF HSV PCR is negative three weeks after onset.
red_herrings.data_point: Bilateral temporal MRI changes with low-grade fever

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Insomnia is a common early feature of anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis; treating it with a hypnotic does not address the underlying process.
red_herrings.data_point: GP prescribed zopiclone for poor sleep and low mood
red_herrings.intended_effect: Stress-related insomnia and anxiety, not encephalitis

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titres related more closely to outcome than serum titres.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumour, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumour removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Extreme delta brush was found in 7 of 23 adults with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis and was associated with a more prolonged illness.
Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions) was frequent in patients with anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis who received them.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

metadata.difficulty_description: Moderate difficulty: 30-year-old man (anti-NMDAR encephalitis is female-predominant but occurs in men). No teratoma. Bilateral temporal FLAIR changes could be mistaken for HSV encephalitis. Empirical aciclovir and immunotherapy must start before the antibody result returns.

patient.chief_complaint: Three-week history of progressive confusion, memory disturbance, and two witnessed convulsions

family_history: No family history of neurological, autoimmune, or psychiatric disease. Father has hypertension.

medications.indication: Insomnia (short course prescribed by GP 10 days before admission)

past_medical_history: Mild upper respiratory tract illness 4 weeks prior to symptom onset, self-limiting

patient.history_present_illness: A 30-year-old secondary school teacher was brought to the emergency department by his wife after a second witnessed generalised tonic-clonic seizure. His wife reported that over the preceding three weeks he had become increasingly forgetful and confused, losing track of conversations and on one occasion failing to recognise the route to his own school where he had taught for four years. He had also begun behaving oddly at home, making repetitive purposeless movements with his hands, and on several occasions repeating the same question within minutes without apparent awareness that he had just asked it. In the week before admission his personality had changed noticeably: he became irritable, suspicious, and at one point accused his wife of hiding things from him. His wife initially attributed these changes to work-related stress as he was preparing students for national exams. He had been seen by his GP approximately ten days before admission with complaints of poor sleep and low mood; the GP had prescribed a short course of zopiclone 7.5 mg at night and planned mental health follow-up. Two days before admission he had a brief (60-second) convulsive episode witnessed by his wife from which he recovered over about 20 minutes, and a second more prolonged (2-minute) seizure on the morning of admission prompted emergency services to be called. In the emergency department he received a 1500 mg IV loading dose of levetiracetam. He had no past psychiatric history. He described a mild sore throat and low-grade fever approximately four weeks prior to onset that resolved without treatment. There is no family history of neurological or psychiatric disease. He does not smoke, drinks approximately 8 units alcohol per week, and uses no illicit substances. He takes no regular medications aside from the recently prescribed zopiclone.

neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm equal and reactive. Mild right gaze preference noted but resolves spontaneously. No obvious visual field defect. Fundoscopy normal.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Confused and disoriented. Oriented only to name. Echolalia noted: repeats examiner's last words. Unable to follow two-step commands. Intermittent automatisms, with repetitive hand fumbling and lip smacking during examination.
neurological_exam.motor: Power 5/5 all limbs. Normal tone. No pronator drift.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Hyperreflexic throughout, with bilateral ankle clonus (3-4 beats). Bilateral extensor plantar responses.
